title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 97 (Tribunal power to call an annual general meeting)

content.overview: If a company defaults in holding an annual general meeting under section 96, the Tribunal may, on application by any Member, call or direct the calling of the AGM and give ancillary or consequential directions. Such directions may include deeming one Member present in person or by proxy to constitute the meeting. A meeting called, held and conducted in accordance with the Tribunal's order is deemed duly called, held and conducted.

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 97 (Power of Tribunal to call annual general meeting). If a company defaults in holding an AGM under section 96, the Tribunal may, notwithstanding anything in the Act or articles, on application of any Member of the company, call or direct the calling of the AGM and give ancillary or consequential directions it considers expedient. Directions may include that one Member present in person or by proxy constitutes the meeting. A meeting called, held and conducted in accordance with the Tribunal's order is deemed duly called, held and conducted. Section 97 is the specific remedy for AGM default; section 98 addresses impracticable company meetings other than AGMs. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Trigger and application
sections.body: Where default is made in holding an AGM under section 96, the Tribunal may, notwithstanding anything in the Act or articles, act on an application by any Member of the company.

sections.heading: Tribunal directions
sections.body: The Tribunal may call or direct the calling of the AGM and give ancillary or consequential directions it considers expedient, including a direction that one Member present in person or by proxy shall be deemed to constitute the meeting.

sections.heading: Effect of compliance
sections.body: A meeting called, held and conducted in accordance with an order under section 97 is, for all purposes, deemed to be a meeting of the company duly called, held and conducted.

sections.heading: Distinction from section 98
sections.body: Section 97 addresses default in holding an AGM. Section 98 addresses impracticability of calling or holding a company meeting other than an AGM in the prescribed manner.

hypotheticals.question: When should section 97 be distinguished from section 98?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 97 is the specific route for default in holding an AGM under section 96. Section 98 concerns impracticability of calling or holding a company meeting other than an AGM in the prescribed manner.

misconceptions.correction: The section deems a compliant meeting duly called, held and conducted.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming the Tribunal's order must always require a minimum quorum of multiple Members.
misconceptions.correction: The section permits a direction that one Member present in person or by proxy constitutes the meeting.
